Salamanders and snakes with two white lines or short tails are ordered killed, house snakes spared; five harmful animals, rats included, may be killed in the Sanctuary or Ihram.
A woman entered Hell for starving a cat, a prostitute was forgiven for watering a dog, a prophet was rebuked for burning ants, and needless dogs cost a Qirat daily.
Allah created Adam sixty cubits tall and sent him to greet the angels, whose reply became his offspring's greeting; Paradise's people will have his form, and people have shrunk since.
Um Sulaim asks whether a woman must bathe after a wet dream, and the Prophet says yes if she sees discharge, which explains why a child resembles its mother.
Abdullah bin Salam asks three things only a prophet knows, accepts Islam on the answers, and the Jews, who had called him their best, then call him their worst.
But for Israelites meat would not decay, and but for Eve wives would not betray husbands; treat women kindly, for woman is created from a rib that breaks if straightened.
In the womb an angel records a person's deeds, death, livelihood and whether wretched or blessed, and what is written decides whether his last deeds lead to Paradise or Fire.
Allah will ask the least-punished in the Fire if he would ransom himself with the earth, reminding him that in Adam's backbone He asked less: to worship none besides Him.
Every unjust murder carries a share of guilt for Adam's first son, who began the practice of murder.
Souls are like recruited troops: those of similar qualities incline to one another, and those of dissimilar qualities differ.
Every prophet, Noah among them, warned his nation of the Dajjal, but the Prophet adds that he is one-eyed, unlike Allah, and his Paradise will really be Hell.
On Resurrection Day Noah's nation will deny he conveyed the message, and Muhammad and his followers will bear witness for him, explaining the verse on being a just nation.
At a meal the Prophet says on Resurrection Day people will seek intercession from Adam and Noah, who decline, then come to him, and he will prostrate beneath the Throne.
The Prophet recited the verse 'Fahal min Muddakir' in the usual way.
Gabriel opens the Prophet's chest, washes it with Zamzam and takes him up the heavens past Adam, Idris, Moses, Jesus and Abraham; fifty prayers become five, then he enters Paradise.
The Prophet says he was granted victory by the easterly wind As-Saba, while the people of 'Ad were destroyed by the westerly wind Ad-Dabur.
A man rebukes the Prophet for giving Ali's gold to four chiefs; the Prophet foretells among his offspring Quran reciters who leave the religion like an arrow and kill Muslims.
Abdullah heard the Prophet recite 'Fahal min Muddakir'.
Alarmed, the Prophet says an opening has been made in Gog and Magog's wall, warns the Arabs, and says they will perish, despite pious among them, when evil increases.
Adam will be told to bring out 999 of every thousand for the Fire; people are gathered barefoot and naked, Abraham clothed first, and some companions taken to the Fire.
Abraham's plea for his father Azar on Resurrection Day is refused, Paradise being forbidden to disbelievers; the Prophet condemns Ka'ba pictures showing Abraham and Ishmael divining with arrows.
Asked who is most honourable, the Prophet says the most righteous, then Joseph, a prophet son of prophets, and among Arabs those best before Islam, if they understand religion.
Abraham, tall in the Prophet's dream and resembling him, circumcised himself at eighty and lied only thrice, once shielding Sarah from a tyrant; a salamander blew the fire on him.
The 'wrong' that must not be mixed with belief in verse 6.83 means joining others with Allah, the Prophet tells worried companions, citing Luqman's advice to his son.
On Resurrection Day people gathered on one plain will ask Abraham to intercede, but remembering his lies he says 'Myself!' and sends them to Moses.
Abraham leaves Ishmael and his mother near the Ka'ba; she runs between Safa and Marwa, an angel brings forth Zamzam, Jurhum settle, and Abraham and Ishmael build the Ka'ba.
The first mosque built on earth was al-Masjid al-Haram, then al-Aqsa forty years later, and wherever prayer time comes one should pray there.
Seeing Uhud, the Prophet says it loves us and we love it, and declares the area between Medina's two mountains a sanctuary, as Abraham made Mecca one.
The Prophet tells Aisha her people built the Ka'ba short of Abraham's foundations, and he would rebuild it but that they had only recently left disbelief.
Asked how to send blessings on him, the Prophet teaches asking Allah to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and Abraham's family.
The Prophet sought refuge for Al-Hasan and Al-Husain with Abraham's words for Ishmael and Isaac: Allah's perfect words against every devil, poisonous pest and evil eye.
The Prophet says we would doubt sooner than Abraham, who asked to see the dead revived; he asks mercy on Lot, and would have accepted release after Joseph's long imprisonment.
Finding men of Aslam at archery, the Prophet urges the offspring of Ishmael to shoot, as their father was an archer, and says he is with both teams.
Asked who is most honourable, the Prophet says the most Allah-fearing, then Joseph, a prophet son of prophets, and among Arabs those best before Islam, if they understand religion.
The Prophet asks Allah to forgive Lot, who wanted to have a powerful support.
The Prophet recited the verse 'Hal min Muddakir', is there any that will remember.
Salih's she-camel was hamstrung by a man of honour and power; at Thamud's Al-Hijr the Prophet has its well water poured out and forbids entering the wrongdoers' homes except weeping.
Joseph is the honourable son of the honourable Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham; asked who is most honourable, the Prophet names the most Allah-fearing, then Joseph.
In his illness the Prophet insists Abu Bakr lead the prayer despite Aisha's plea that he is soft-hearted, likening her to Joseph's female companions, and Abu Bakr leads.
The Prophet prays for the rescue of Aiyyash and Salama bin Hisham and asks Allah to punish Mudar with years of drought like those in Joseph's time.
